### What is the feedback loop?

The feedback loop describes the process when an employee makes a report, and all of the events that follow, ending with "Closing the feedback loop." This last step is an important, if under-executed, part of the reporting process. Unfortunately, it is often overlooked. According to the Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (AHRQ), this last step in the reporting process is sometimes referred to as 'the black hole' by nurses because it's usually forgotten or ignored. 

### Why is it important?

The safety feedback loop helps ensure accountability, helps ensure that an action was taken (even if that action was only to investigate a matter further), and communicates to hospital staff that their organization takes event reporting seriously and cares about patient well-being. **Below are a few suggestions for improving follow-up:**

- **Direct follow-up or making the rounds**  
Leaders and staff can follow-up directly with event reports, but there is also utility in conducting actions like Walkarounds, which can reveal risks which providers may not yet have reported and give leaders a chance to aid in correcting them and demonstrating their commitment to safety. 

- **Indirect Follow-up**  
Follow-up on problems identified by a number of different staff members can also be communicated back to them via newsletters explaining the issue identified and steps taken to fix it, or through emails sent out to relevant stakeholders.

- **As part of the daily routine**  
Regular in-person meetings during which a few minutes are devoted to discussing common safety events recently reported, and the ways to address such issues, are also very useful. 

>Source: 

>Nuckols, T. Incident Reporting: More Attention to the Safety Action Feedback Loop, Please.  PSNET. Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality (2011). [https://psnet.ahrq.gov/perspective/incident-reporting-more-attention-safety-action-feedback-loop-please](https://psnet.ahrq.gov/perspective/incident-reporting-more-attention-safety-action-feedback-loop-please)
